clue.text: New delivery company admits noon impossible

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new

indicators.note: a company that admits something lets it inside its own name

parts.note: Ocado is a British online grocery delivery firm
N stands for noon

explanation.surface: A start-up courier refuses lunchtime deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: Ocado is a UK online supermarket that delivers groceries; N for noon goes inside it, after N for new. NO CAN DO is the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase is a blunt refusal saying a request simply cannot be managed.

clue.text: Nothing like temperature required for oven

parts.note: zero, shaped like the letter O
as means in the manner of
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: A cook notes that an oven needs heat of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, familiar from the Kent countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop-drying kiln is a kind of furnace, so calling it an oven is fair.

clue.text: Golden river when camping? Son makes floods

indicators.note: camping puts one under canvas, so the preceding words sit inside the shelter

parts.note: what campers sleep in
S abbreviates son
or is gold in heraldry
R abbreviates river

explanation.surface: A golden river glimpsed on a camping trip, with a son looking on, leads to floods.
explanation.walkthrough: The camping word does double duty: it supplies the tent and tells you OR and R go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrents are rushing deluges of water, which is what floods are.

clue.text: Priest cracking nuts has creepy hidden dimension

indicators.note: something cracking a nut breaks into it, so the priest goes inside
nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written for the shuffle
P abbreviates priest

explanation.surface: A priest cracking nuts is somehow linked to a spooky hidden dimension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder along with 'creepy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction uses this term for a further spatial realm beyond our three, through which ships travel faster than light.

clue.text: Fancy secretary, wanting introduction later

indicators.note: the opening letter is wanted further on, so it moves from the front to the back

parts.note: an aide is an assistant or secretary

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a secretary who hopes to be introduced later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is a noun here, as in a notion or whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy can be a passing notion or conceit of the mind, so it matches a thought.

clue.text: State of affairs before man fell — good edge on stair

parts.words: State of affairs before man fell
parts.note: before the Fall in Eden there was no sin
G abbreviates good

explanation.surface: A theological musing on Eden collides with a carpenter's note about stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Before Adam's fall there was NO SIN; add G to get NOSING.
explanation.definitionFit: In joinery the nosing is the rounded projecting front of each tread on a staircase.

clue.text: Hunt employee fighting in play room

indicators.note: the fighting is placed inside the other words' letters

parts.note: a game is play
a den is a small room
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Children fighting in the playroom suggests a rowdy household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' reads as a verb but is a noun here: a hunting estate whose staff include someone guarding the quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A game warden manages wildlife on an estate where hunting takes place and is employed to protect the quarry.

clue.text: Rogue set trap for old barman

indicators.note: a rogue element misbehaves, so these letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A villain lays a trap for a pub landlord of yesteryear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster was the archaic term for someone who drew and served beer in a tavern.

clue.text: Churchill's strength? Love rat Conservative scratching his head

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter of the party word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Musings on a Conservative love rat puzzled about Churchill's virtues.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'love rat' phrase is tabloid slang, but it splits into O and RAT. The question mark marks Churchill as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was famed for his wartime speeches, so skill in public speaking was his great strength.

clue.text: Model French couture in the morning, then American

parts.note: Christian Dior, the Paris fashion house
a.m. means before noon
A abbreviates American

explanation.surface: A catwalk model wears French couture in the morning, then something American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a fashion model, but it is a miniature scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scale scene, as in a museum display, so it is a kind of model.

clue.text: Entertainer in part works cutting fringes

indicators.note: trimming the fringes removes the letters at both edges

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A performer has a role in a play about factory work being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' belongs to the definition: an entertainer playing a part.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a performer who takes on a role, so an entertainer cast in one.

clue.text: Candidates noticed huge screen revolving after start of election

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of election

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the words before it are read backwards

parts.note: seen means noticed
IMAX is the giant-screen cinema format

explanation.surface: Election candidates are spotted on a huge rotating screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candidates' suggests politicians, but here they are people sitting an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates in an examination are those being tested, the people sitting it.

clue.text: Be self-defeating, like your special French accent?

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
something special to you is one's own
the grave accent, as on è

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a person's distinctive French accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like your special French accent' reads as a question about pronunciation, but accent means the written mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about your own downfall through your own actions is to defeat yourself.

clue.text: Skin condition with slime, oil and pus, not for everyone

indicators.note: a film for everyone is rated U, so not for everyone drops that letter

parts.note: goo is slimy matter
sebum is the skin's natural oil
taken as written
joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A grim description of a skin complaint involving slime, oil and pus, unsuitable for squeamish readers.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all, so 'not for everyone' removes it from PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosebumps are the pimpled skin that appears with cold or fear, a passing condition of the skin.

clue.text: Promise small children claiming attention a puzzle

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the following word is held inside

parts.note: giving your word is a promise
S abbreviates small
CH is a dictionary abbreviation for children
to have someone's ear is their attention

explanation.surface: Someone promises small children who want attention a puzzle to keep them busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' and 'children' are two abbreviations that together form the outer shell, with the attention word inserted between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wordsearch is a grid of letters in which hidden words must be found, a popular puzzle type.

clue.text: Road so winding one turns the wrong way

indicators.note: a winding path twists about, so these letters twist into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A road winds so much that a driver turns the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a cricket term: a doosra is a ball from an off-spinner that turns the opposite way to his usual delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A doosra is a spinning cricket delivery that breaks against the bowler's normal direction, deceiving the batsman.

clue.text: Turbulent race invades to seize power

indicators.note: seizing something grips it, so the other letters surround power

parts.note: raids are invasions
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A violent people invades a land to seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like an ethnic group, but it means a fast current of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapids are stretches of fast, broken river water, and a race is a strong current.

clue.text: Defendant's statement certain to provide amusement

parts.note: a defendant enters a plea of guilty or not guilty
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A defendant's confident statement in court provides some amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or entertainment, which is what amusement offers.

clue.text: Psychological relief to find employment for child taking year off

indicators.note: taking off a year removes the letter that abbreviates year

parts.note: to place someone is to find them a job
a boy is a child

explanation.surface: A parent finds relief in finding work for a child on a gap year.
explanation.walkthrough: Y abbreviates year, so it leaves BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert treatment whose benefit comes only from the patient's belief in it.

clue.text: As reported, area of smooth ice will form ridges

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is about sound

parts.note: a skating surface plus the contraction of will

explanation.surface: A news item warns that the ice rink surface will develop bumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' is not a link word; spoken as 'll it ends the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrinkle is to crease or pucker, making small folds or furrows on a surface.

clue.text: European wrongly placed Leicester in the north

indicators.note: letters placed wrongly are out of order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the shuffle
N abbreviates north; the rest taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has mistakenly put the English city of Leicester in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester is in the English Midlands, which is why placing it north is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liechtensteiner is a native of the small Alpine principality, so a European.

clue.text: Sexy couple's bedtime accessory

parts.note: hot means sexy
to couple is to tie together

explanation.surface: An amorous couple's bedtime accessory is hinted at.
explanation.walkthrough: Hottie also means an attractive person, which the surface plays on; here it is British slang for a hot-water bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-water bottle warms a bed before sleep, an item used at bedtime.

clue.text: E.g. crabs caught turn orange one by one

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to rust is to go an orange-brown colour
an ace is a one in cards
a means one

explanation.surface: Crabs that are caught and cooked turn orange one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The two ones give different pieces, ACE and then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs belong to the class of hard-shelled arthropods, so they are an example of the group.

clue.text: Sharp knife with a point

parts.note: to knife is to cut
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A sharp knife comes with a pointed tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks like the knife's edge but means clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean shrewd or clever, especially in American usage, which matches sharp.

clue.text: Reception starts at last, almost without guests

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped
at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of starts
with no company is alone

explanation.surface: A reception finally begins, but almost nobody has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' is a word to take a letter from, not a beginning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a reception room or a gathering held in one, as in a fashionable soirée.

clue.text: Perhaps earth live element

parts.note: L marks the live wire on a British plug
air is one of the four classical elements

explanation.surface: It reads like a list of plug wiring: earth, live, element.
explanation.walkthrough: On a British plug the terminals are marked L (live), N and E (earth), so 'earth' and 'live' look electrical; here an earth is a fox's den.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's burrow is called an earth, and that is one example of an animal's den.

clue.text: One advocating dunking bread is limited by having no drink

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

indicators.note: being limited by something means being bounded on both sides by it

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who likes dunking bread finds it a limitation having nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a soft round bread roll in Britain; a teetotaller is abbreviated with the two-letter initials of 'total abstinence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptists practise full immersion baptism of believers, so they advocate a ritual dunking.

clue.text: My face is friendly

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
dial is slang for a face

explanation.surface: Someone says their own face is a friendly one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation here, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial describes warm and amiable behaviour, the manner of someone sociable towards others.
